opportunities.title: Small grants

amount.raw: Awards vary according to project but will only exceptionally exceed £6,000 and will generally fall in a range of £1,500-£5,000. Travel and subsistence up to £2,000 per person for trips up to 13 days, up to £2,500 per person for 14 days or more; up to £5,000 for PhD fieldwork visits of six months or more; Japan office up to ¥300,000 for PhD students.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants must belong to, or provide evidence of support from, an organisation or institution willing to receive grant funds. Applications not accepted from individuals seeking support for personal projects, though the UK office may consider individuals with proof of organisational support. Grant payments cannot be made to personal bank accounts.
opportunities.summary: Seed funding to enable UK-Japan projects that might otherwise not be possible, bringing people in the UK and Japan together to deepen mutual understanding, encourage exchange of ideas or expertise, or develop lasting collaboration. Supports festivals, workshops, performances, exchanges, collaborative projects, Japanese language teaching, and academic research/visits/exchange.

opportunities.title: Butterfield Awards in Medicine and Health

deadlines.raw: 1 December (decision in March of the following year)

amount.raw: Up to £10,000; continuing projects lasting up to three years to a maximum of £10,000 per year, to a total limit of £30,000.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to health and medical professionals, researchers, practitioners, policy makers, managers and voluntary sector workers in both countries. Applicants should normally show an existing research record. Project must involve partners in both the UK and Japan. Preference given to those not previously involved in UK-Japan collaboration and early-career applicants.
opportunities.summary: Supports exchanges and collaborations between health and medical professionals in Japan and the UK, including study of scientific, clinical, social and economic issues in healthcare. Grants may be used for travel expenses or to contribute to other costs including conference and publication costs.
